Root.value / defaultValue.semantic: identifies WHICH ITEM is open (item value, not a boolean). Non-nullish = open, nullish = closed.

Root.orientation.semantic: drives which arrow keys move between items and which keys open the popup.

Root.onOpenChangeComplete.semantic: fires after the closing animation (the only open-state callback on Root).

Root element/nesting.type: renders <nav> at the root, <div> when nested
Root element/nesting.semantic: nest a second Root inside a higher-level Content for multi-level menus.

List / Item / Trigger / Icon.type: List renders <ul>; Item renders <li>; Trigger renders <button> (disabled prop, default false); Icon renders a span
List / Item / Trigger / Icon.semantic: Trigger opens on hover or click; Icon carries data-popup-open for rotation.

Content.keepMounted.semantic: keeps content in the DOM while closed (helps SSR/crawlers).

Positioner.type: UseAnchorPositioningSharedParameters (side, align, sideOffset, alignOffset, anchor, collisionAvoidance, collisionBoundary, collisionPadding, sticky, positionMethod, arrowPadding) + data-instant
Positioner.default: same anchor-positioning defaults as other Positioners
Positioner.semantic: positions the popup against the currently active trigger; also exposes --positioner-width/--positioner-height CSS vars and a --duration/--easing animation pattern in the docs example.

Popup.type: renders <nav>; children include Arrow and Viewport
Popup.semantic: the popup is the animated container; docs pattern: <Popup><Arrow/><Viewport/></Popup>.

Viewport.semantic: clipping viewport of the current content; animate it for size/opacity transitions.

Link.semantic: emits data-active; use `render` for framework links.

Portal.semantic: optional; omit to render inline in the DOM.

Backdrop / Arrow.semantic: Backdrop is the overlay; Arrow points at the active trigger.

dataAttributes: Content: data-open, data-closed, data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-activation-direction ('left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down')
Popup: data-open, data-closed, data-starting-style, data-ending-style, data-anchor-hidden, data-side, data-align
Positioner: data-open, data-closed, data-anchor-hidden, data-side, data-align, data-instant
Arrow: data-open, data-closed, data-side, data-align, data-uncentered
Root / List / Item / Portal / Viewport: none
renderProp: Shared `render` contract on every part (ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement, plus state-driven className/style). The docs' custom-link example renders `<NavigationMenu.Link render={<NextLink/>}/>` for client-side routing. Custom primitives: useRender; merging: mergeProps/mergePropsN.
controlled: `value` / `defaultValue` (default null) + `onValueChange(value, eventDetails)`. There is NO `open`/`onOpenChange` on the Root — open-ness is derived from whether `value` is non-null, and `onOpenChangeComplete(open)` is the only open-state notification. `actionsRef` -> { unmount }.
keyboard: List stops propagation of the main-orientation arrow keys (horizontal: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight; vertical: ArrowUp/ArrowDown) so focus moves between top-level items (NavigationMenuList.mjs). Trigger opens the popup with ArrowDown when horizontal, or with ArrowRight/ArrowLeft (RTL-aware) when vertical (NavigationMenuTrigger.mjs, reason 'list-navigation'). Hover opens after `delay` (50 ms default) and closes after `closeDelay`; Escape/outside press/focus-out close it (reasons in the ChangeEvent union). Once open, focus is managed by the popup; there is no typeahead for top-level items and no PageUp/PageDown handling.
notableDifferences: React Aria ships no equivalent navigation-menu primitive (you compose `Disclosure`/`Popover` or a Menu), so there is no 1:1 source API: Base UI models the open item as a `value` (+`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`) instead of `open`/`onOpenChange` booleans, and hovering is first-class with `delay`/`closeDelay` (default 50/50).

Composition is mandatory and verbose: Root > List > Item > Trigger + Portal > Positioner > Popup > (Arrow, Viewport) — the content only animates correctly when it lives inside `<Viewport>` inside `<Popup>` inside `<Positioner>`; the docs' 'Large menus' section also describes dropping Portal/Positioner for inline nested submenus (use `defaultValue` so a nested menu can start open).

Nesting a Root inside a Content switches the rendered element from <nav> to <div> and creates a second-level menu with the same value semantics ('Nested inline submenus' example omits the nested Portal and renders List + Viewport with a defaultValue).

Animated content switching is exposed through data-activation-direction ('left'|'right'|'up'|'down') on Content plus --positioner-width/--positioner-height and --transform-origin CSS variables, with a data-instant escape hatch on the Positioner — React Aria uses different transition-state APIs.
Link is the only element with data-active; there is no data-selected/data-current vocabulary.
